fields: What should an architect define before selecting Claude architecture components?
The measurable business outcome, constraints, and success criteria.
Why is “we need an AI agent” not a complete requirement?
It names an implementation preference rather than the underlying outcome and constraints.
Which requirements should remain deterministic when correctness must not depend on probabilistic output?
Hard rules such as authorization, numeric thresholds, and schema validation.
Why is a production Claude system more than a model call?
Because the request path also includes identity, context, tools, state, verification, outputs, observability, and recovery.
What should be designed alongside the happy path?
The failure and recovery path.
What should remain authoritative for current transactional facts?
The system of record, not chat history, a vector index, or a cached summary.
What distinguishes a workflow from an agent in Anthropic's architecture guidance?
A workflow follows predefined code paths; an agent dynamically decides how to accomplish the task and use tools.
When is a workflow generally preferable to an agent?
When the process can be enumerated in advance and benefits from predictability and control.
When is an agent justified?
When required steps cannot be reliably predetermined and dynamic planning/tool use provides measured benefit.
What is the orchestrator-worker pattern?
A lead agent decomposes work, delegates bounded subtasks, and synthesizes worker results.
What are strong reasons to use multiple agents?
Context isolation, parallel independent work, and meaningful specialization.
What is prompt chaining?
A sequence where each stage consumes the previous stage's output.
What is routing?
Classifying an input and sending it to the appropriate specialized path.
Why is model-token cost alone insufficient for architecture comparison?
Total solution cost also includes engineering, infrastructure, human review, monitoring, incidents, and compliance overhead.
What must exist before claiming a business improvement?
A baseline and measurable outcome.
Outcome requirement
The measurable value or change the solution should create.
Risk constraint
A condition defining what the system must not do without stronger controls.
System of record
The authoritative source for current operational state.
Idempotent retry
A retry that can safely repeat without duplicating an unintended side effect.
Workflow
LLM/tool orchestration through predefined code paths.
Agent
A system where the model dynamically directs its own process and tool use.
Orchestrator
The component that interprets the goal, decomposes work, delegates, and synthesizes results.
Context isolation
Keeping independent worker contexts separate to reduce interference and pollution.
Parallelization
Run independent subtasks concurrently and combine their results.
Routing
Classify an input and send it to the appropriate specialized path.
Technical metric
A system measure such as task success, latency, throughput, token use, or cost per task.
Business metric
An outcome such as time saved, cases resolved, error reduction, revenue impact, or customer satisfaction.
Architecture should begin with the {{c1::business outcome}}, not the preferred AI component.
Hard authorization rules belong in {{c1::deterministic controls}} rather than relying only on prompts.
Convert vague goals into {{c1::measurable targets}} before choosing a model or pattern.
For stateful workflows, define {{c1::state ownership}} explicitly rather than treating model context as durable state.
Design the {{c1::failure path}} at the same time as the happy path.
Current transactional facts should come from the {{c1::system of record}}.
A {{c1::workflow}} follows predefined paths, while an agent dynamically chooses its process.
Prefer the {{c1::least autonomous}} pattern that still meets the requirement.
Multi-agent systems are justified by meaningful {{c1::isolation, parallelism, or specialization}}, not by novelty.
The orchestrator should verify {{c1::coverage and worker outputs}} before synthesis.
Use {{c1::parallelization}} only when subtasks are genuinely independent.
An {{c1::evaluator-optimizer}} loop needs measurable evaluation criteria, not vague critique.
Before claiming improvement, define a measurable {{c1::baseline}}.
Compare architectures using {{c1::total solution cost}}, not model-token cost alone.

Non-functional requirements

System of record

Workflow

Agent

Orchestrator-workers

Context isolation
What decomposition pattern classifies a request and sends it to a specialized path?
Routing
What term describes the starting measurement used to quantify improvement?
Baseline
